summary: KEP-1027 proposes standardized union (oneOf) semantics for Kubernetes API types, using a discriminator field plus union member markers, so the API server can validate that only one member is set and normalize client intent. Its status is implementable at stage alpha, implementable from 2020-12-30.
rationale: Union semantics are implicit in core types (e.g. VolumeSource, DeploymentStrategy), so clients cannot reliably understand them and the server cannot normalize objects written by version-skewed clients. The KEP relies on server-side apply (#555) and does not aim to migrate all existing unions. Later comments show the work was repeatedly deferred across releases, and a 2025 comment says the normalization and validation code paths were still not implemented.

summary: KEP-378 (Kubernetes Bootstrap Checkpointing) proposed checkpointing annotated control-plane pods to the filesystem via a kubelet flag, --bootstrap-checkpoint-path, gated as Alpha. Its recorded status is implemented, stage stable, from 2020-12-29; the discussion concerns the status/stage labelling rather than the feature design.
rationale: The design goal was to record annotated Pods to the filesystem and have the kubelet load them on restart, to enable self-hosting. The status of "implemented" with stage "stable" was assigned retroactively during a 2021 KEP cleanup (PR #3007), which the sources say skipped PRR review. Participants disagreed on whether it should be "implemented" or "implementable", and the sources do not record a final resolution beyond the status shown.

summary: KEP-2377 proposed a declarative kustomize format to expose imperative kubectl transformation functionality (configmap/secret generation, cross-cutting labels/annotations/names, strategic-merge patches) within declarative workflows. Its status is implemented, stage stable, and kep.yaml records that it is replaced by KEP-2386 Kustomize Subcommand Integration.
rationale: Gaps in kubectl force users to write scripts to preprocess declarative config, even though most needed transformations exist as imperative kubectl commands. The KEP addresses this by giving users a declarative format to reach those capabilities. The sources do not explain why KEP-2386 superseded it. The 2021 PR #3007 discussion about marking KEPs as implemented concerns status rules and does not address this replacement.

summary: KEP-2263 proposes a plan for testing the scalability and performance of Kubernetes storage components, measuring overhead of sig-storage controllers, kubelet volume manager and CSI sidecars across volume types and dimensions (max volumes per pod, node, cluster). Its status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale: The KEP addresses the lack of known scale limits and SLOs for the Volume API. The stated motivation is to understand current limits, set expectations for consumers, and find bottlenecks. The discussion notes that some tests were implemented but more follow-up is needed, and that no PD tests were running yet.

summary: KEP-2129 proposed deprecating and removing cAdvisor v1 JSON metrics (ContainerInfo and MachineInfo endpoints) from the kubelet, as a step toward removing cAdvisor APIs from the kubelet. Its status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: cAdvisor only supports Linux and a small set of runtimes, so sig-node wants vendors to replace cAdvisor without double-collection cost. The JSON endpoints were already disabled by default from 1.18 and re-enableable via --enable-cadvisor-json-endpoints, and the KEP re-visits removal given concerns raised about removing them permanently. Out of scope: Prometheus cAdvisor metrics, the Summary API, and the kubelet's cAdvisor dependence.

summary: KEP-1435 proposed relaxing Kubernetes API validation so that a type=LoadBalancer Service can declare ports with different L4 protocols (e.g., UDP and TCP on the same port number), with cloud provider LB controllers determining the actual exposure. The status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Users wanted one IP address exposing multiple L4 protocols, but the API rejected mixed-protocol LoadBalancer Services because some clouds bill per protocol. The KEP proposed removing that validation restriction and analysing how billing and backing load balancer capabilities would be affected per cloud, with the option to make the feature configurable. The excerpt does not record the final implementation details or the outcome of that analysis.

summary: KEP-980 adds a service.kubernetes.io/load-balancer-cleanup finalizer to Services of type LoadBalancer so the Service is not fully deleted until the cloud load balancer resources are cleaned up. Its status is implemented at stage stable, set from 2020-12-16.
rationale: Service controller can leave orphaned load balancer resources after a Service is deleted, which customers reported repeatedly. The proposal blocks Service deletion with a finalizer until cleanup finishes, and rolls it out in phases so downgrades stay safe. The sources in this record do not explain the status label itself beyond a PR-process dispute over whether implemented requires a PRR file.

summary: KEP-5030 proposes making cluster-autoscaler aware of CSI volume attach limits when simulating scale-up (via templated CSINode objects for upcoming nodes), and having the kube-scheduler NodeVolumeLimits plugin refuse pods needing a CSI volume on nodes lacking that driver, but only when a cluster admin explicitly opts in via CSIDriver. Status is implementable, stage beta.
rationale: Cluster-autoscaler ignores CSI attach limits for upcoming nodes, so it packs too many volume-using pods per node and undershoots scale-ups. The scheduler plugin also treats a missing CSINode as unlimited, letting pods land on nodes before their drivers publish. The KEP fixes CA simulation and makes the scheduler behaviour opt-in so that CA and scheduler changes stay decoupled and default behaviour is preserved.

summary: KEP-789 proposed removing the system:unauthenticated subject from the default system:discovery and system:basic-user ClusterRoleBindings, and adding a new public-info-viewer ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding so that /healthz, /version and /version/ stay unauthenticated. The KEP is marked implemented at stable stage.
rationale: The CVE-2018-1002105 post-mortem and privacy concerns about CRD exposure through default discovery bindings motivated hardening the defaults. The KEP keeps unauthenticated access to a small set of non-sensitive endpoints that legitimate use cases depend on. The sources do not explain the implementation history in detail; the discussion mainly covers the later status-label cleanup.

summary: KEP-5589 proposes removing Kubernetes' runtime and generation-time dependencies on the unmaintained gogo protobuf library by defining local interfaces for the methods API machinery uses, stripping unused generated protobuf code, and moving go-to-protobuf rewrite logic into a maintained generator. Status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale:
Gogo protobuf has been unmaintained since 2021, so any future vulnerability or bug fix would require replacing it first, and its runtime references propagate to all Kubernetes module consumers. The generated code also misleadingly appears to implement standard protobuf interfaces that Kubernetes does not actually use, risking runtime panics. The KEP keeps the serialization code unchanged and leaves non-protobuf Go type behavior unchanged, while removing the gogo references.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

summary: KEP-3614 proposes that kubeadm start adding new etcd members as learners (etcd learner mode, introduced in etcd 3.4) instead of as voting members, gated by a new EtcdLearnerMode feature gate that graduates over a year or more.
rationale:
Members added as voting members can disrupt cluster quorum if they are faulty, and kubeadm joins from slow control plane nodes have required manual removal with etcdctl. Learner mode means a faulty new member would not disrupt quorum. The KEP adds a learner code path behind a feature gate and plans to deprecate and remove the old path after graduation.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">Status is provisional, stage beta, so the source gives no final outcome. The excerpt does not say why the KEP is at this stage.

summary:
KEP-495 added an opt-in pod-level `ShareProcessNamespace` boolean so all containers in a pod share one PID namespace, with CRI updated to support Container, Pod and Node PID modes. The feature was hidden behind a feature gate, which was later removed in 1.19, and the KEP is recorded as implemented at stable stage.</summary>
<parameter name="rationale">The design addresses the lack of PID namespace sharing between containers in a pod, which had been an implicit API relied on by some images. The default of false keeps per-container PID namespaces, so existing `pid == 1` expectations stay backward compatible. A maintainer later reported the feature complete after the feature gate was removed in 1.19.

KEP-491 covers kubectl diff, which shows how applying a configuration would change the live cluster state. The KEP is retroactive: it documents a feature implemented before the KEP process, and its status is Implemented at stable stage.
rationale: The feature let users see how configuration changes would affect the cluster before applying them, which the design calls "a key piece of declarative configuration management." The authors considered four diff variants and chose "current live" to "future" configuration because that "describes exactly the changes that are happening on the cluster." The KEP's goal is stated as "mostly retroactive, since the feature has mostly been implemented before this process existed."

summary: KEP-902 adds an optional Preempting (PreemptionPolicy) field to PriorityClass and PodSpec so pods of a given priority can wait in the scheduling queue without preempting lower-priority pods. The status is implemented at stage stable; the feature went GA in 1.24.
rationale: Batch workloads with backlogs of unscheduled pods could have partially completed work discarded when higher-priority pods preempt them. The KEP makes preemption optional per PriorityClass, defaulting to true for backward compatibility. The field is copied into PodSpec at admission so the scheduler does not need to read PriorityClasses. Per the discussion, the GA graduation (PR #3110 and related k/k and k/website PRs) was completed in 1.24.

summary: KEP-2053 exposes hugepage requests and limits (all page sizes) through the downward API, gated by the DownwardAPIHugePages feature gate on the apiserver side, with the kubelet supporting it regardless of the gate. Status is implementable, stage stable.
rationale: Pods could not read their hugepage request or limits via the downward API, unlike cpu, memory, and ephemeral-storage. The change loosens API validation, so all kubelets must support it before the apiserver accepts its use, which is why a KEP was written. Reviewers agreed that new standard resource types should have downward API coverage as part of alpha/beta criteria.

summary: KEP-2221 proposed deprecating and then removing dockershim (the built-in Docker CRI) from the kubelet code base. The KEP is recorded as implemented, stage stable, with implemented-from date 2022-08-09.
rationale: Dockershim ran inside kubelet and was tightly coupled to its lifecycle, so kubelet depended on a specific container runtime and runtime CVEs burdened sig-node and administrators. The design aims to deprecate and remove it. The discussion shows the removal was tracked for the 1.24 release, and a 2022-05-10 comment states the KEP was fully implemented in 1.24.

summary: KEP-4580 proposed deprecating kubelet RunOnce mode, marking the KubeletConfiguration RunOnce field and --runonce flag as deprecated, and later removing the flag and mode. The KEP stayed provisional at alpha; the author closed the tracking issue in July 2024 and later said the KEP no longer needs updating.
rationale: RunOnce mode does not work in systemd mode, lacks support for newer pod features such as init containers and volumes, and has no e2e or integration tests. Reviewers asked for a deprecation path that is gradual and feature-gated, and for PRR and risk sections, while the v1.31 code PR missed code freeze due to a merge conflict. The sources do not give a final reason for dropping the KEP beyond the missed freeze and the author's later comment.
outcome_reason: The provisional status is the recorded fact. The issue was closed by the author on 2024-07-24 after the enhancement was removed from v1.31 at code freeze, and the author later said "We don't need to update this KEP anymore." The sources do not explicitly say why the author chose not to continue.

summary: KEP-5732 adds topology-aware and DRA-aware workload scheduling to kube-scheduler, evaluating candidate "Placements" (node/DRA subsets) for whole PodGroups. Its current status is implementable, stage beta; during review the DRA-aware implementation was moved to beta, while topology constraints are the alpha-scope focus.
rationale: The problem is that the default pod-centric scheduler cannot resolve group-level topology constraints (e.g., co-locating a PodGroup in one rack), and external tools like Kueue or Volcano decouple that decision from the scheduler. The KEP proposes embedding Placement evaluation into the scheduler, reusing existing pod-level filter and score plugins. Reviewers narrowed the scope: the author moved DRA-aware implementation to beta to wait for KEP-5729 to define PodGroup-level ResourceClaims. The status was advanced from provisional to implementable on 2026-02-10 after a sig-scheduling maintainer asked for the change.

summary: KEP-383 graduates the new Event API (events.k8s.io/v1) to GA. The API was promoted from v1beta1 to v1 in 1.19, with only kube-scheduler migrated to use it at the time of the excerpt.
rationale: Existing Events are spammy, have unclear semantics, and can overload the API server. The new API makes semantic fields first-class for better deduplication and querying, adds series detection that sends only start and finish events, and uses a more aggressive backoff. Reviewers settled that the API itself has no feature gate, and that the client-library fallback to the old API is kept while the library is used across many clients.

summary: KEP-5295 proposes KYAML, a strict subset ("dialect") of YAML, as a new kubectl output format (`-o=kyaml`) and as the preferred format for project documentation and examples. The KEP status is implemented, stage stable.
rationale: Conventional block-style YAML is whitespace-sensitive and has type-coercion traps (e.g. "NO" parsed as bool, "11:00" as a sexagesimal number), which make hand-editing and templating (e.g. Helm) error-prone, while JSON lacks comments. KYAML uses flow style with always-double-quoted values, unquoted safe keys, and {} and [] delimiters so it is not whitespace-sensitive and remains valid YAML. The KEP states it is not required of users and that existing YAML output is retained.
